limitations: This is lexical source inspection, not elaboration, a successful Lean build, an axiom dependency audit, or independent proof verification.
Custom syntax, imported dependencies, toolchain/compiler trust, generated expressions, and parser edge cases require separate review.
Quoted strings are omitted, including interpolated strings; custom elaborator and metaprogramming tokens remain separately reported.
The scan is limited to the original repository src/*.lean files. It does not inspect the implementations of external Lean/Mathlib dependencies.
Absence of a listed token is not evidence that the formal theorem has the intended mathematical meaning.

reviewed_findings.assessment: kexactB elaborates a term and assigns it to a goal. kcopy recursively builds terms by projections/constructors and assigns them; its probe calls Kernel.isDefEq. cpt_copy_thms substitutes names in existing definition/theorem types and values, then calls addDecl for defnDecl/thmDecl. These are material metaprogramming audit points; their presence alone is not evidence of an unchecked axiom. Successful kernel checking was not established.
The five run_cmd/modifyEnv occurrences add namespace strings to Lean.LibrarySuggestions.nameDenyListExt. They do not visibly add theorem or axiom declarations.

Of 32 run_tac occurrences, 30 use liftMetaTactic/revertAll followed by exact an existing declaration. FramesTildeGammaValues.lean constructs a Subsingleton.elim proof and notes it. ExistsGIs.lean assigns the local hypothesis h to the goal. This source inspection does not establish kernel acceptance of the resulting terms.

87 macro keyword occurrences are recorded. Inspected declarations expand quoted Lean term/tactic syntax, including wrappers around kexactB. This is a lexical inventory, not a proof that every macro is semantically faithful.

37 allowUnsafeReducibility true occurrences are present. Other audit-relevant options include hygiene false (31), quotPrecheck false (7), and backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false (1877). These are not the debug.skipKernelTC option; this audit does not infer successful kernel verification from that distinction.

main_theorems_original:
import Formalism.GammaFactorNonvanishing.CritLine
import Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.CharacterBoxes.ClaimStrip
import Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.CharacterBoxes.MainConclusion

open Complex DirichletCharacter

theorem allChi : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter := UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter

theorem rhOfAll : RiemannHypothesis := Formalism.VW.rh_of_every allChi

theorem critAll (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (hχ : χ.IsPrimitive) (s : ℂ)
    (h0 : 0 < s.re) (h1 : s.re < 1) (hz : LFunction χ s = 0) : s.re = 1 / 2 :=
  Formalism.VW.critLine allChi N χ hχ s h0 h1 hz

theorem claimAll : Claim.HalfPlane ∧ Claim.Strip ∧ Claim.Zeta :=
  ⟨allChi, Claim.strip allChi, Claim.zeta allChi⟩

readme_excerpt.text: # Riemann Hypothesis in Lean — by Levent Alpöge (with Claude)
> **The proof in this repository is the work of [Levent Alpöge](https://alpo.ge/).**

> On 2026-11-20 he announced that, working with Claude, he had found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis that extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (for Dirichlet L-functions), and that the argument is fully formalized in Lean without assumptions.
> All credit belongs to Levent Alpöge (and Claude). This repository is an unmodified mirror of the Lean code he published, put on GitHub so that people and agents can browse, clone and check it.
**Status.** As of mirroring (2026-11-20), no independent build or review of this code has been published. Treat it as a claimed proof until it has been compiled and checked.
The `src/` tree in this repository is byte-for-byte the content of that archive; this README, `.gitignore` and nothing else were added.

The mathematics and the Lean code are by **Levent Alpöge**, working with Claude. The original archive was published at https://alpo.ge/ without a stated license; this mirror adds no license of its own and claims no authorship. If the author asks for this mirror to be changed or removed, it will be.

provenance.assessment: The README attributes the mathematics and Lean code to Levent Alpöge working with Claude. It says no independent build/review had been published as of mirroring, asserts byte-for-byte correspondence to the original archive, and states the original archive had no stated license and this mirror adds none. This audit has not independently compared the original web archive. A permissive redistribution license is not established; preserve the attribution/no-license notice and do not relicense the source as Apache/MIT without a separate grant.
